thread:
maria: Hey team — escalated ticket from a customer: embeddings/v1 endpoint throughput dropped ~4x since yesterday evening. They say tokens/sec looks stable but vectors/sec plummeted. GPU queue depth high in our metrics. Can someone help triage?

raj: Is this customer on hosted or dedicated? Any model change?

maria: Hosted (standard). They were on model=embed-large-1536-v2. No config change on their side per the customer. They attached a sample request and timings.

sophie: Pasted their sample timings from their support note: 
```
single request (1 vector): 120ms
batched 8 vectors: 1.1s (expected ~300ms)
throughput reported: ~200 vecs/sec => used to be ~800 vecs/sec
```
Looks like batching not scaling.

henry: GPU metrics show queue_depth spike around 2025-11-05T22:10Z for that tenant's shard. Utilization low-ish (~40%) but NVLINK copies spiking. Kernel occupancy low. Classic sign of many small batches or sync waits.

raj: Could be a dimension mismatch causing fallback to CPU path or an unoptimized kernel. Any logs with DimensionMismatchError?

maria: Customer included one error in logs: `WARN model-runner: output-dim mismatch expected=1536 got=768` — they said it happened a handful of times.

sophie: That looks like two model variants in the routing pool: one 1536-dim embed (new) and one 768-dim (older). If requests route to the wrong variant, postprocessing might be trying to reshape and failing then falling back to slower path.

raj: Good catch. Also could explain tokens/sec steady but vectors/sec drop — model returns shorter vectors or extra postproc overhead. Can we check routing table for the customer's tenant and whether recent model rollout occurred? @deploy-bot any deploys to embed-large pool around that timestamp?

deploy-bot: deploy event: 2025-11-05T21:58Z — rolled out embed-large-1536-v2 to pool embed-large-prod-03 (canary->gradual).

maria: Customer reports problem started ~22:05Z which lines up.

henry: I pulled per-instance logs on pool embed-large-prod-03. There are a handful of messages where the kernel library warns about incompatible model shapes and then we see an extra CPU-side quant-unpack step: 
```
W kernel: model_shape != expected_shape, performing cpu_slowpath()
cpu_slowpath: dequantize -> reshape -> memcpy
```
This adds ~20-40ms per batch, which multiplies with many small batches.

raj: Also check batch_sizing telemetry. If batch_size fell from 32->6 because of token distribution, throughput will drop disproportionately. Any queue_depth histograms?

sophie: Queue histograms show avg batch size dropped from 18 to 5 for that shard starting at 22:00Z. Concurrent inflight windows increased (more tiny batches).

maria: Customer's integration uses dynamic batching with batch_hint=auto. They recently changed client to send more frequent small requests (spike in qps but smaller per-request). Could be client side.

raj: Repro steps I ran from our side against the same model in staging: 
- curl single request: 95ms
- python concurrent 16 workers sending 1 vector each: total throughput 230 vec/s
- python send 16 concurrent requests batching into 8-per-batch (explicit): 780 vec/s
So behavior matches: many tiny concurrent requests collapse throughput.

maria: Customer insists they didn't change frequency much. They did upgrade their SDK last week though.

henry: Two risk vectors: 1) rollout introduced mixed model variants in the same pool -> occasional dim mismatch + fallback, and 2) client-side request size distribution changed -> smaller effective batch sizes. Both together amplify the regression.

raj: Short term mitigations: 
- rollback embed-large-1536-v2 canary from pool embed-large-prod-03 to avoid mixed shapes (sophie/infra).
- add temporary model-shape routing guard to reject incompatible dims rather than fallback (runtime) so failures are loud and customer's client will see errors instead of slower results (henry/eng-runtime).

sophie: I can roll back the canary from that pool now. Doing it in 2 minutes and monitoring queue depth.

maria: I'll tell the customer: "we've identified a likely mixed-variant routing issue coinciding with your observed regression. We're rolling back to previous pool variant and will follow up with repro steps. If you still see poor perf, please send a few sample request timestamps and your SDK version."

henry: I'll open a follow-up task for eng-runtime to add a guard and also add a telemetry tag when cpu_slowpath is triggered so we can correlate with tenant.

raj: For repro/next actions, I documented steps for support to reproduce locally: 
1) run this script against embed-large-1536-v2 in staging: 
```python
# quick benchmark
import requests, time, threading
URL='https://staging.api.redwood/v1/embeddings'
def send_once():
    r = requests.post(URL, json={"input": ["a"]})
    return len(r.json()[0])

# concurrent tiny requests
threads=[]
for _ in range(16):
    t=threading.Thread(target=send_once)
    threads.append(t); t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
```
2) compare with explicit batching (send list of 64 inputs) and compare vectors/sec.
3) Run `rtctl metrics tail --filter pool=embed-large-prod-03` and look at `batch_size_histogram` and `cpu_slowpath_count`.

maria: Nice. I'll attach that to the ticket with suggested timeline and ask them to try explicit batching as a workaround.

sophie: Rollback complete at 2025-11-05T22:22Z. Initial metrics: queue_depth dropping back to normal within 2 minutes, avg batch size climbing back to ~16.

henry: telemetry shows cpu_slowpath_count for that pool dropped to near zero after rollback. Good signal.

maria: Customer confirmed they see throughput improving to ~760 vecs/sec now. They were happy to get runtime back.

raj: Follow-ups: 
- eng-runtime to implement shape-guard + explicit failure mode (P1) — henry will coordinate.
- infra: improve deploy canary isolation so mixed-dim models don't share same pool (sophie owns).
- support: ask customer to prefer explicit batching or SDK version rollback if they still see variance.

henry: I'll file the runtime ticket and link to this thread.

maria: Thanks all — closing the escalated ticket as customer verified improvement. Leaving thread open for eng action items. :thumbsup:
